cards.text: Chronicles has been rolling out family lines like dough with no end, and now it's the clans of Judah, one of Jacob's sons: Perez, Hezron, Hur, Ashhur the father of Tekoa with his two wives, and a sister named Hazzelelponi. HAZZELELPONI. Friend, I tried saying that out loud and my mustache tied itself in a knot.
Then, in the middle of all these names, the record slows down for one man: Jabez, more honorable than his brothers. And after Hazzelelponi, a name I can actually say? I already LIKE him.

cards.question: Jabez's mother is the one who named him. What reason does she give for the name Jabez?

answers.text: He was born in a strange land
He was born during a famine

cards.question: Jabez, the man named for his mother's pain, calls out with a big request. Who does he call out to?
In his prayer, Jabez asks God to bless him and enlarge his territory.
Jabez asks God's hand to be with him and keep him from harm, so that he will be free from ___.
God turns down the request of Jabez.

cards.text: Then the record picks right back up with Judah's clans: a town called Ge-harashim, named that because its people were craftsmen, Mered, whose wife was Bithiah, Pharaoh's daughter, plus linen workers, and potters who lived in the service of the king. Craftsmen, linen workers, potters. Whole families known for what they MADE, and meanwhile my one skill for years in that junk drawer was collecting DUST.

Next comes the family line of Simeon, Judah's brother and another son of Jacob: Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers didn't have many children, so the clan never got as numerous as Judah's. They live in towns like Beersheba and Ziklag, and they keep a record of names. Twenty-two children! I raised six little cookie cutters and I STILL needed a nap.
Those Simeonite clan leaders? Their families increased greatly, and somebody's group chat just hit two hundred members and NOBODY knows who half of them are.

cards.question: With their families growing, the Simeonites journey to the entrance of Gedor, east of the valley. They're searching for ___ for their flocks.
At Gedor, the Simeonites find land that's crowded and full of trouble.
The record says someone had lived at Gedor before the Simeonites showed up. Who was it?

cards.text: Now the record jumps ahead to the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah, when the men named in that list attack the Hamites in their dwellings, and the Meunites who were there too. Friend, the record doesn't soften it one bit: they devote them to destruction.

cards.question: After the attack, the Simeonites settle in that land at Gedor. What reason does the record give?

answers.text: There was pasture for their flocks
The king had ordered them to stay
The cities there had strong walls

cards.text: And that's not the end of it. Five hundred Simeonites head out, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.

cards.question: Where do the five hundred Simeonites go?
At Mount Seir, the five hundred Simeonites strike down the remnant of the ___ who had escaped.
After the battle, the Simeonites stay at Mount Seir, and the record says they have lived there to this day.

findings.problem: This story card is not the opening card, but it has 3 sentences: the summary of verses 11-23, 'Craftsmen, linen workers, potters.' and the junk drawer joke. The first sentence is also hard to follow, with Ge-harashim, Mered and Bithiah, the linen workers and the potters all strung together with commas.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card is not the opening card, but it has 4 sentences: Shimei's children, the towns and the record, 'Twenty-two children!' and the cookie cutter nap joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke is joined to the Bible fact with 'and' ('Their families increased greatly, and somebody's group chat just hit two hundred members'). It reads as if the group chat and the made-up number 'two hundred' are part of what happened. That makes the comparison confusing, and it doesn't click right away as a separate everyday image.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The card says 'the record jumps ahead to the days of Hezekiah,' which adds a time gap between the journey to Gedor (4:39-40) and the attack (4:41). Verse 41 says 'These who were noted by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah.' It never says the attack came later than the journey, and the text reads as the same event. The time link should stay as open as the text leaves it.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
